pr_title: ESQL: Add support for TEXT fields in comparison operators and SORT
pr_body:
(Refactoring of #98317, extending the operators instead of modifying QL module)

This fix adds support for TEXT fields in comparison operators (`==`, `!=`, `>`, `>=` etc., including LIKE and RLIKE) and in SORT command.

The fix consists in passing one more parameter to `BinaryComparison`, `Order` and `RegexMatch` constructors (and all the subclasses) to define whether the instance should resolve on TEXT fields (for ESQL) or not (for SQL and EQL).

Operators pushdown (both for filtering and sorting) is enabled only if the property also declares an [exact multi-field](https://www.elastic.co/guide/en/elasticsearch/reference/current/multi-fields.html) that can be used as a fallback, otherwise the optimization gets skipped and the operation is executed in-line.

[edit]

Added a rule that replaces fields with their exact subfield when possible

Fixes #98642

issue_context.title: ESQL: exact operation should use the exact field if available
issue_context.body:
### Description

A common scenario is having strings indexed both as text and as keywords - doing a stats on the former is very expensive (due to extraction from the source) and is likely to timeout while the latter works as expected.
Similar to SQL, the planner should identify the scenario and replace the field accordingly with the exact subfield.

review_comments:
Why is this needed? Aren't the operators performing their own, full type resolution?
In fact why still have this rule in place?
Why are both job and job.raw extracted? Wouldn't job.raw be enough or does jaw leak somewhere?

In the initial version of this PR, I [replaced all the occurrences](https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/pull/98528#discussion_r1304628316) in the plan with their exact subfield (including `EsRelation`), and as a result there was no need to load `job` anymore, but it made the planning a bit more convoluted, with the addition of some [aliases](https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/pull/98528#discussion_r1304629376) to keep the original names (otherwise the output for `from idx` would result in `job.raw` instead of `job`).
There could be a smarter way to do it and avoid fetching TEXT fields; in case we can further investigate and do it with a follow-up PR (at low level there are other optimizations, so we should not load from _source anyway)
What purpose does this method serve; in particular where it is being used?

It's used in two tests that check the output based on the mapping. 
Before this change, it was just `mapping.keySet()`, but now the mapping also contains a TEXT field with a KEYWORD subfield, so we have to take it into consideration as well.
